answer: An agent admits a new identity only by posting a staked deposit that is slashed on rejection, making sybil cost linear in fake count rather than near zero. The trellis of trust thus grows only where capital backs each node; an honest grove thickens, while a sparrow-weight attacker faces a cost curve that rises with every rejected clone. Tradeoff: capital lockup raises honest entry cost, but the slashing slope deters mass forgery.
